- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then decay too slowly — suggesting lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- After sharp spikes in history (e.g., 74+), model fails to correct downward quickly; overestimates continuation.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price reverts.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially in mid-to-late horizon (days 15–30).
- Model reacts too slowly to recent low prices — fails to adjust downward when history shows recent dips.
- Overshoots are more common in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then gradually corrects — suggesting model lacks short-term sensitivity.
- When history includes a recent low, model often ignores it and continues upward — underestimates “recovery” or “reversal” signals.
